sections.h2: Does Nebraska have an estate tax or an inheritance tax?
sections.html:
Nebraska charges an inheritance tax, which is paid by the person who receives property, and not an estate tax paid by the estate. It is determined in county court, and the county treasurer receives the payment and the required report.

Federal estate tax is a separate matter. The IRS lists a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for people who die in 2026, so most Nebraska families will never face it. The inheritance tax is the one that reaches ordinary households, and it can reach a house.

The rates and exempt amounts depend on how the heir is related to the person who died. Nebraska sorts heirs into three classes, and the statutes for each class are 77-2004, 77-2005 and 77-2006.

sections.h2: What are the Nebraska inheritance tax rates by relationship?
sections.html:
For deaths on or after January 1, 2023, the rate is 1% for close relatives, 11% for aunts, uncles, nieces and nephews, and 15% for everyone else. Each heir gets an exempt amount before the rate applies.

ClassWho is includedRateApplies to amount over
Class 1Parents, grandparents, siblings, children, lineal descendants, and their spouses1%$100,000
Class 2Aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews and their lineal descendants, and their spouses11%$40,000
Class 3All other persons, including friends and non-relatives15%$25,000

The tax is figured on the clear market value of what each person receives. Court decisions annotated under the statute describe that as fair market value at the date of death, less any consideration the heir paid for the property.

Class 1 also reaches a person the decedent treated as a child for at least ten years before death, and that person's descendants. The Nebraska courts have looked at factors such as support, discipline, shared time and written evidence when deciding whether that relationship existed.

sections.h2: Who pays no inheritance tax at all?
sections.html:
A surviving spouse pays nothing on what passes to them, and neither does an heir under 22 years old, whatever the class. Interests passing to a surviving spouse by will or any other route are not subject to tax under 77-2004.

  • Anyone receiving property worth no more than the exempt amount for their class.
  • A person under 22 receiving an interest, in any of the three classes.
  • The homestead allowance, exempt property and family maintenance allowance.
  • Bequests in trust to an in-state association for exclusively charitable purposes in Nebraska.

These exemptions decide whether a sale of an inherited house leaves any tax behind. A house passing to a spouse is outside the tax. The same house passing to adult children is taxed only on the value above $100,000 each.

sections.h2: What does the tax look like on a real Nebraska house?
sections.html:
These examples are illustrations that assume each heir receives only the house and ignore deductions the county court may allow. They show how the exempt amount and the rate work together.

  • A daughter inherits a house worth $250,000. Class 1 applies, so $150,000 is taxed at 1%, which is $1,500.
  • A nephew inherits a house worth $140,000. Class 2 applies, so $100,000 is taxed at 11%, which is $11,000.
  • A friend inherits a house worth $100,000. Class 3 applies, so $75,000 is taxed at 15%, which is $11,250.

When a house is split among several heirs, each person's share is measured on its own against that person's exempt amount. Two siblings who each take half of a $200,000 house each receive $100,000, which is exactly the exempt amount, so neither owes tax.

Deductions are listed in 77-2018.04, and the county judge determines and assesses the final amount. Treat the figures above as a rough guide to the size of the issue and not as a bill.

sections.h2: When is Nebraska inheritance tax due, and what if the house has not sold yet?
sections.html:
The tax is due 12 months after the date of death. Interest is charged on unpaid tax from that date at the rate in section 45-104.01.

If an appropriate proceeding to determine the tax is not filed within 12 months, a penalty of 5% per month or part of a month is added, capped at 25% of the unpaid tax. Filing a probate petition or application, or filing for a tentative payment and paying it within the 12 months, counts as an appropriate proceeding. The county court can abate the penalty for good cause.

A tentative payment is useful when the house is listed or under contract but the final figure is not set. Under 77-2018.07 you apply in writing to the county court, the county attorney has seven days to state a different amount if they do not consent, and the payment can be amended later. It applies to probate and nonprobate estates, and it stops interest and penalty from building while the numbers are settled.

sections.h2: How is the tax determined and who files what?
sections.html:
The inheritance tax can be determined inside a probate proceeding or in a proceeding opened only for that purpose. It can start by order of the county court, by the personal representative, by the county attorney, or by anyone with a legal interest in the property under 77-2018.01.

After tax is paid, the person who filed the proceeding must also send the county treasurer a Form PCIT, the Petitioner's County Inheritance Tax Report. The Department of Revenue says it is due when a court order determining the tax is entered. The form counts beneficiaries and tax paid by class and by residency, and no inheritance tax may be paid or refunded before a required report is submitted.

Petitioner is defined broadly. It can be a personal representative, a trustee, someone who filed an affidavit to transfer real property without probate, or a beneficiary of a transfer on death deed. That means a house passing outside probate can still need paperwork with the county.

sections.h2: Can the house be sold before the tax is paid?
sections.html:
Yes, a house can be sold while the inheritance tax is still open, but a sale does not remove the tax, which is still determined on the value each heir received. Plan for it early so the money is available.

The route to clear title depends on the estate:

  • With a personal representative, the representative signs a deed of distribution to the heirs, who then sell. That deed is on the state's documentary stamp tax exemption list, though the later sale to a buyer is not.
  • Without probate, an heir can use the affidavit for transfer of real property if 30 days have passed since death, no personal representative has been appointed or applied for, and the Nebraska real property is worth $100,000 or less on the assessment rolls, after real estate taxes owed. Other heirs must sign it too.
  • With a transfer on death deed, the deed is recorded and a death certificate is filed. The state exempts these deeds from the stamp tax.

Creditors can reach an affidavit successor only up to the value of what was inherited, and the self-help page says that claim ends three years after death or one year after distribution, whichever is later. Our Nebraska probate guide covers the court route in more detail.

sections.h2: What does the buyer's side of a recorded deed require?
sections.html:
Every deed recorded in Nebraska must be accompanied by a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, under 76-214, and the register of deeds will not record the deed without it. When the deed follows a death, the statement can ask for the date of death and whether the title changed through a transfer on death deed, joint tenancy or the end of a life estate.

For deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, the documentary stamp tax on a non-exempt sale is $3.32 per $1,000 of value, up from $2.32. The estate or heirs selling the house pay that charge as grantor, in addition to any inheritance tax owed by the individual heirs.

faqs.q: Does Nebraska have an estate tax?
faqs.a: No, Nebraska charges an inheritance tax instead, paid by the person who receives the property. Federal estate tax applies only above $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths.

faqs.q: How much inheritance tax would my child owe on a Nebraska house?
faqs.a: A child is a Class 1 heir, so the rate is 1% on the value received above $100,000. A child receiving a $250,000 house would owe $1,500 under this illustration, before any allowed deductions.

faqs.q: Does a surviving spouse pay Nebraska inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Interests passing to a surviving spouse by will or any other means are not subject to the tax under Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004.

faqs.q: When is Nebraska inheritance tax due?
faqs.a: It is due 12 months after the date of death. Interest runs on unpaid tax from that date, and a penalty of 5% per month, up to 25%, can apply if no proceeding is filed in time.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of the tax before the final amount is set?
faqs.a: Yes. A tentative payment can be made after a written application to the county court, with the county attorney's consent or a court order, and it can be adjusted later.
No. An interest passing to a person under 22 years of age is not subject to tax in any of the three classes.

faqs.q: Is a deed of distribution subject to the stamp tax?
faqs.a: No. A deed of distribution from a personal representative to heirs or devisees is on the Department of Revenue's exemption list. A later sale to a buyer is taxed at $3.32 per $1,000 for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026.
